summary: Otto Spies specialized in religious studies and Indology, earning a Ph.D. under Enno Littmann at Tübingen and a Dr. juris at Bonn. He served as professor at Aligarh Muslim University (1932–1936), Breslau (1936), and Bonn (1951–1971).

Otto Stein worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned degrees under Heinrich Swoboda and Moriz Winternitz at Charles University and the German University in Prague, where he later served as Privatdozent (1922) and professor of Indology (1930–1939).

Otto Strauss, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, studied at Munich, Berlin, and Kiel, completing his Ph.D. under Hermann Oldenberg. He held posts at Kiel University (1911, 1920), the University of Calcutta (1913–1920), and the University of Breslau (1928–1935).
Otto Stursberg was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD at the Humboldt University of Berlin around 1904–1907 under the supervision of Richard Pischel.
Otto Walter was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Strasbourg by 1903 under doctoral supervisor Ernst Leumann.

Indologist Otto Wecker studied at the universities of Berlin, Münster, and Tübingen, where he earned his PhD under Richard von Garbe around 1903–1905. He later taught at the University of Göttingen from 1947 to 1953.

Indologist and linguist Otto von Böhtlingk studied at Saint Petersburg, Berlin, and Bonn under Franz Bopp, Christian Lassen, and A. W. von Schlegel. He served at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences (1842–1868) and the University of Jena (~1868–1885).

Otton Ottonovič Rozenberg worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Saint Petersburg under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy, earning a Ph.D., and at Bonn and Berlin, later becoming a professor at Saint Petersburg State University in 1919.
Owen Flanagan is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fordham University and Boston University. Around 1996, he became Professor of Philosophy at Duke University.

Owen Lattimore was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Harvard University (1928–1929) and held a post at the University of Leeds from around 1963 to 1970.

P. A. Payutto is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned a bachelor's degree at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, serving there as Associate Dean (~1964–1974). In 1995, he held the post of Tipitaka Acharaya at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.
P. Anujan Achan was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya. He served as Government Archaeologist at the Thrissur Zoo and State Museum.
P. B. Meegaskumbura worked in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, serving as a professor at the University of Peradeniya (attested in 1991 and 2010).

Scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy P. D. Premasiri earned degrees at Peradeniya, Cambridge, and Hawaiʻi (PhD under Eliot Deutsch). He spent decades at the University of Peradeniya, including serving as department head (1997–2004) and professor (attested 2010).

P. De Lacy Johnstone was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh, as well as the University of Oxford and Balliol College, where he was a Boden Sanskrit Scholar and earned a B.A. and M.A.
P. H. Joshi was an Indologist who served as a Research Officer at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1976–1988), where he was also attested in 2002.

P. K. Mukhopadhyay worked in philosophy and Indology. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and was a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 2009).

P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under A. Chinnaswami Sastri. He served as an Assistant at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1941) and as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1963).

Pramod P. Joglekar is an archaeologist and Indologist. He served on the Regulating Council and as editor at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (2020–2025) and is Professor of Bioarchaeology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).

Indologist P. P. Subrahmanya Sastri studied at the University of Madras and the University of Oxford. He served as Curator of the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library (attested 1937) and Professor at Presidency College, Chennai (attested 1937–1944).
